name: Can I stay within my home while the roof is removed?

mainEntity.name: Is it ever safe or practical to live in the house during the phase when the roof is opened for a second-story addition?
mainEntity.text: Is it ever safe or practical to live in the house during the phase when the roof is opened for a second-story addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Living in the house while the roof is removed is usually not practical for most families. Once the roof is opened, the home becomes vulnerable to dust, noise, weather exposure, and security concerns. Some contractors can install temporary protection or build the project in phases, but that does not always make the house comfortable or safe enough for daily living. The risk level also depends on the season, the quality of temporary weatherproofing, and whether utilities are still running normally. In projects where the upper floor is built above occupied space, the work can also create constant vibration and movement through the house. Even if a homeowner technically can remain in the property, the experience is often stressful and disruptive. Before deciding to stay, ask the builder for a clear plan showing how the home will be protected each week, what areas will be off-limits, and how long the roofless phase will last.
